messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel rollout we see +18% p95 latency on Mixtral MoE tails. Suspect kernel selection + KV cache fragmentation. Posting short profile and suggested next steps.
tara: Link to logs?
alex: Pasting quick profile snapshot (tail of perf). Not exhaustive, but shows where time moved: 
```
hotspots:
 - kernel: fast-softmax-v3 (64%) -> per-token 0.32ms
 - kernel: rope-rewrite (15%) -> per-token 0.12ms
 - kv-serialize (12%) -> per-request 0.28ms
 - router (9%) -> per-request 0.14ms
```
alex: Also observed a big RoPE compute spike once seq > 1024 — looks like numeric/scale mismatch with the quantized kernel path.
mike: Interesting. Did the kernel selector heuristic change? Maybe it prefers v3 for short seqs but is falling back incorrectly for MOE expert patterns.
linh: Notes: v3 does aggressive head fusion and assumes head_dim in {64,256}. When head_dim=128 we hit the slowpath which increases memory traffic.
alex: Exactly — Mixtral experts are non-uniform in head_dim due to per-expert fusion differences, so kernel v3 misclassifies some expert work and forces fallback.
perf-bot: Benchmark completed: canary(5% traffic) p95 delta +17% for rollout fast-softmax-v3 — more details at /perf/2934
tara: Ok. What's the experimental plan?
mike: My proposal: 
 - rollback kernel to fast-softmax-v2 on canary
 - run KV pressure sim with per-expert hotset=512 to reproduce thrash
 - router temperature sweep [0.6,0.8,1.0,1.2]
 - A/B increase topk from 2 -> 4 to see load distribution
linh: +1, also add KV cache affinity: pin hot keys to contiguous expert shards to reduce fragmentation.
sanjay: We should check quantization path differences too — v3 uses int8 kernels with different rounding semantics which can change RoPE phases.
alex: Good call. Add a numeric parity regression for RoPE on long sequences (>=2048).
tara: Can you paste the commands to reproduce the sim?
alex: Sure: 
```
# run MoE sim with stress config
./tools/run_moe_sim --model mixtral --hotset 512 --kernel fast-softmax-v2 --topk 4 --router_temp 0.8
# collect perf trace on server
perf record -o /tmp/trace.data -p $(pidof inference_server) -- sleep 30
perf script > /tmp/trace.txt
```
mike: I can spin up the canary with that config at 11:00 PST. @perf-bot schedule Canary:fastsoftv2-11:00
perf-bot: scheduled Canary:fastsoftv2-11:00 for channel eng-runtime
linh: Minor observation: router logits show more noise when topk=2 -> some experts starve. topk=4 reduces variance and evens out per-expert KV pressure.
alex: Action items prioritized: 1) pin kernel=v2 on 5% canary 2) KV affinity sim + mem-profile 3) router temp sweep + report 4) topk=4 A/B. I'll add RoPE parity test to CI.
tara: I'll own dashboards: latency / per-expert time / kv hit rate / cost delta. Also adding alert on per-expert p95 > 1.5x baseline.
mike: 👍 will update here once canary runs.
